notifications.silent: This build shows no notifications: only the installed app does, or a build started with {{variable}}=1. The counts on the app's icon still update.

needsYou.title: Needs you
needsYou.hint: An agent asks, a plan or a run waits for you
needsYou.description: An agent waits for your approval, an answer or a message, or a plan or a run waits for your decision.

stopped.title: Stopped
stopped.hint: A run stops at a limit, a runner goes offline
stopped.description: A run stopped at a limit or was interrupted, a project's runner is offline, or a merge stopped.

finished.title: Finished and info
finished.hint: A run ends or fails, a merge lands
finished.description: A run is ready to merge, was merged or failed, a plan limit reached 90% or was reset, or the Orchestrator proposes something.

sound.title: Sound
sound.description: Notifications play the system's notification sound.

quiet.title: Quiet hours
quiet.hint: No sound and no banners between these times
quiet.description: No notifications between these times each day. The count on the app's icon still updates.
quiet.same: Choose two different times: these quiet hours are not taken.

notifications.notSaved: Your notification settings were not saved: {{reason}}

dailyReport.title: Daily report from the Orchestrator
dailyReport.hint: What was done, what waits and tokens, in its chat
dailyReport.description: Each day at this time, every open project's Orchestrator conversation gets a report of what was done that day: merges, runs, what waits for you, what the Orchestrator did and the day's tokens. A day without activity gets none; a report missed while the app was closed comes at its next start. With Let the Orchestrator answer agents on, the Orchestrator adds a summary that only proposes.
dailyReport.unreadable: Whether the daily report is on cannot be read: {{reason}}
dailyReport.notSaved: Your daily report setting was not saved: {{reason}}

automation.onlyYou: Only you, here in the window

lookAtWindow.title: Look at the window
lookAtWindow.hint: Screenshots, the element tree, the app's log and state
lookAtWindow.description: Screenshots, the element tree, the app's log and state. Every client with the token may.

windowControl.title: Agents can control this window
windowControl.hint: Click, type, resize, change pages · applies from the next start · only you can change this
windowControl.description: Click and type in this window, resize it, change pages and the theme. Turn it on to let an agent test Orchester.
windowControl.notSaved: Window control could not be kept: {{reason}} This run keeps what it started with.
windowControl.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.
windowControl.buildRelease: Build default: off in release builds like this one; development builds start with it on. A change applies when Orchester starts again.
windowControl.buildDevelopment: Build default: on in development builds like this one, so design checks can drive the window; release builds start with it off. A change applies when Orchester starts again.
windowControl.chosenOn: Your choice: on for this run. A change applies when Orchester starts again.
windowControl.chosenOff: Your choice: off for this run. A change applies when Orchester starts again.
windowControl.nextStartOn: On from the next start. Until Orchester starts again, agents can't click or type in this window.
windowControl.nextStartOff: Off from the next start. Until Orchester starts again, agents can still click and type in this window.
windowControl.environmentOn: This run: on, set by {{variable}}=on. The setting here applies when Orchester starts without that variable.
windowControl.environmentOff: This run: off, set by {{variable}}=off. The setting here applies when Orchester starts without that variable.

answerApprovals.title: Let automation answer approvals
answerApprovals.hint: Approve once or deny; wider answers stay yours
answerApprovals.description: Clients may approve a waiting tool request once or deny it, recorded as answered by automation. Wider answers stay yours. Off until you turn it on.
answerApprovals.on: Each answer reads approved by automation or denied by automation in the run, with the client's name.
answerApprovals.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

changePermissions.title: Let automation change agent permissions
changePermissions.hint: Widen write access, network, commands, MCP servers
changePermissions.description: Lets tools connected to Orchester widen what agents may do: write access, network, commands, MCP servers, approving automatically, new CLI programs and environment variables. Applies to setup tools and permission confirmations in the window; automatic approvals also need Let automation answer approvals. Secret replacement and stale-version decisions stay yours. Only you can change this, here in the window.
changePermissions.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

publishDrafts.title: Let the Orchestrator publish drafts
publishDrafts.label: Publish drafts
publishDrafts.hint: Pipelines, profiles, instructions, skills and tools it drafts
publishDrafts.description: Lets the Orchestrator's chat publish the pipelines, agent profiles, instructions, skills and tools it drafts, without your click. Off: it proposes each publish as a card you apply. A draft that widens what agents may do still needs Let automation change agent permissions. Only you can change this, here in the window.
publishDrafts.on: The chat publishes without asking in every project and keeps each publish as an action in its conversation. A draft that widens what agents may do is still proposed while Let automation change agent permissions is off.
publishDrafts.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

answerAgents.title: Let the Orchestrator answer agents
answerAgents.label: Answer agents
answerAgents.hint: Read their questions and answer, or tell you with a recommendation
answerAgents.description: Lets the Orchestrator's chat answer agents' questions and send messages to a run's agents without your click, and start a turn by itself when an agent asks or waits for a message. Off: it proposes each answer as a card you apply, and tells you when an agent waits. Approvals and plan decisions stay yours. Only you can change this, here in the window.
answerAgents.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

mergeRuns.title: Let the Orchestrator merge runs
mergeRuns.label: Merge runs
mergeRuns.hint: When you ask it in the chat
mergeRuns.description: Lets the Orchestrator's chat merge a run you asked it to merge, without your click: only a task's latest run that succeeded, and only when the main checkout needs no local integration. Off: it proposes each merge as a card you apply. Conflicts and approving a merged result stay yours, on the Local integration page. Only you can change this, here in the window.
mergeRuns.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

mergeFinished.title: Let the Orchestrator merge finished runs on its own
mergeFinished.label: Merge finished runs on its own
mergeFinished.hint: Without asking, when every step passed
mergeFinished.description: When a task's run succeeds, the Orchestrator's chat merges it without your click: only the task's latest run whose every step passed (a step you accepted as it was counts, one automation accepted does not), never a task marked Blocked or blocked by unfinished tasks, while new starts are held, or for a task that says Don't merge automatically, and only when the main checkout needs no local integration. It tries each run once, one at a time in the order they finished; conflicts it proposes to send back to an agent, anything else it leaves to you. Needs Let the Orchestrator merge runs and Let the Orchestrator answer agents on too. Off: it tells you a run is ready and the merge stays yours. Only you can change this, here in the window.
mergeFinished.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

continueInterrupted.title: Let the Orchestrator continue interrupted runs
continueInterrupted.label: Continue interrupted runs
continueInterrupted.description: Lets the Orchestrator's chat continue a run that a crash, the runner going away or quitting the app interrupted, from its last checkpoint, without your Continue. With Let the Orchestrator answer agents also on, it continues such a run once when it is interrupted, but leaves one interrupted again within 10 minutes to you. Off: continuing stays yours, on the task's Summary. Runs stopped at a limit, runs you canceled and runs whose worktree is gone stay yours. Only you can change this, here in the window.
continueInterrupted.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

writeGit.title: Let the Orchestrator write with git
writeGit.label: Write with git
writeGit.hint: Commit, branch, pull and push when you ask it to
writeGit.description: Lets the Orchestrator's chat commit, create and switch branches, pull, push, merge, revert, tag and fetch in the project's repository when you ask it to. None of these loses work: a switch keeps your changes or is refused, a pull only fast-forwards unless you ask for a merge, a push never forces, and a conflict is undone. Reset, clean, deleting a branch or tag, a forced push, discarding changes and rebase stay cards you apply, whatever this says. Never in a run's worktree before the run ended. Off: the chat only reads git. Only you can change this, here in the window.
writeGit.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

enabled.title: Let agents connect to Orchester
enabled.hintOff: Agents you registered can't reach Orchester until you turn this on
enabled.description: Agents and tools on this computer reach Orchester at a fixed address, each with the access token. What they may do is set below. Off: nothing listens.
enabled.off: Agents and tools on this computer reach Orchester at a fixed address, each with the access token. Off: nothing listens; agents you registered can't reach Orchester until you turn this on.

address.title: Address
address.hintListening: Listening · agents registered with it reach this app
address.hintFixed: Fixed, so an agent you register once keeps connecting after Orchester restarts.
address.description: Fixed, so an agent you register once keeps connecting after Orchester restarts. If the port is taken, Orchester says so here and doesn't move to another one.
address.off: Nothing listens while the server is off. The address and the token stay as they are.
address.none: No address while the server is not running.

port.label: Port
port.taken: Port {{port}} is in use by another program, so Orchester isn't listening. It doesn't move to another port on its own: agents registered with this address would reach nothing. Choose another port, then register your agents again.
port.changed: Now listening on port {{port}}. Agents registered with port {{old}} need registering again.
port.refused: Windows refuses port {{port}}, so Orchester isn't listening: it keeps the port for itself (Hyper-V, WSL or Docker reserve ranges of ports), or another program holds it exclusively. It doesn't move to another port on its own. Choose another port, then register your agents again.

token.title: Access token
token.whereWindows: Kept in Windows Credential Manager, never in a file. Agents send it with every request. Only you can show, copy or rotate it, here in the window.
token.whereMacos: Kept in your login keychain, never in a file. Agents send it with every request. Only you can show, copy or rotate it, here in the window.
token.shownFor: Hidden again in {{seconds}} s. While it shows, the MCP server refuses screenshots and the window's text, so no agent reads it.
token.copied: Copied. Orchester clears it from the clipboard in 1 minute if it's still there.
token.copyFailed: The token could not be put on the clipboard.

rotateConfirm.title: Rotate the token?
rotateConfirm.agents: Every agent registered with the current token stops connecting until you register it again with the new one.
rotateConfirm.sessions: Open sessions end now. The new token replaces the old one in {{store}}.

token.rotated: New token in use. Register your agents again with the commands below; for Codex, set ORCHESTER_APP_MCP_TOKEN again.
token.notRotated: The new token couldn't be stored in {{store}}: {{reason}} The current token stays in use.
token.unreadable: The token can't be read from {{store}}
token.unreadableBody: {{reason}} The server is off until it can be read; agents keep their registration. Try again, or rotate the token to store a new one.
token.notRead: The token can't be read from {{store}}: {{reason}} Show and Copy need it.

server.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change the MCP server's settings, here in the window.
server.unavailable: The server did not start. The log says why.

copy.title: Server
copy.qa: This copy listens on a new port on each start, with a token of its own for this run. Clients find both in its discovery file.
copy.development: This development build listens on a new port on each start, with a token of its own for this run. Clients find both in its discovery file.
copy.qaNote: This copy was started for QA: a new port on each start; its discovery file is in {{folder}}. The address and token settings apply to normal starts.
copy.developmentNote: Development build: its discovery file is {{file}}. The installed app keeps its fixed address, so both can run at once.
copy.developmentNoFile: Development build: it writes no discovery file while it is not listening. The installed app keeps its fixed address, so both can run at once.

connect.title: Connect an agent
connect.hint: Registers Orchester in the agent's CLI
connect.description: Register Orchester once in your agent's configuration. The agent then has Orchester's tools in every session, as mcp__orchester__…: no process id, no file to read.

claude.user: Copy puts the command with the token on the clipboard; Orchester clears it after 1 minute. Run it in a terminal, then check with claude mcp get orchester. Never put the token in a repository's .mcp.json.
claude.local: Run it in that folder. Claude Code keeps it in ~/.claude.json, outside the repository. There's no project option: it would write the token into the repository's .mcp.json.
claude.copied: Copied with the token. Orchester clears it from the clipboard in 1 minute if it's still there. Run it in a terminal, then check with claude mcp get orchester.

codex.step1: Register Orchester in Codex. Codex reads the token from a variable, not from its configuration:
codex.step2Windows: Set the variable for your user. It reaches programs started after this, so restart Codex, your terminal or your IDE:
codex.step2Macos: Set the variable for your user. launchctl setenv reaches apps started from the Dock or Finder until you sign out; add the same export to ~/.zshrc for terminals:
codex.readersWindows: setx keeps the variable in your Windows user profile, and every program you start from then on gets it, so other programs running as you can read the token. Agents in Orchester's runs never get it: their environment is cleaned. After Rotate token, set it again. Check with codex mcp get orchester.
codex.readersMacos: The variable is in the environment of every program you start from then on, so other programs running as you can read the token. Agents in Orchester's runs never get it: their environment is cleaned. After Rotate token, set it again. Check with codex mcp get orchester.
codex.alternative: Or put the token in ~/.codex/config.toml instead (no variable; any program running as you can read that file):
codex.copied: Copied with the token. Orchester clears it from the clipboard in 1 minute if it's still there.

connect.unavailable: The commands need the access token, which can't be read now.

connected.title: Agents connected
connected.description: Since Orchester started. Names and versions are what each client says it is.
connected.descriptionRotated: Since the token changed. Names and versions are what each client says it is.
connected.none: No agent connected since Orchester started.
connected.noneRotated: No agent connected since the token changed.

theme.descriptionWindows: Dark or light colors, or the appearance Windows has when Orchester starts.
theme.descriptionMacos: Dark or light colors, or the appearance macOS has when Orchester starts.
theme.noteWindows: System doesn't follow a change made while Orchester runs yet: if Windows switches between light and dark, the window keeps its colors until Orchester starts again.
theme.noteMacos: System doesn't follow a change made while Orchester runs yet: if macOS switches between light and dark, the window keeps its colors until Orchester starts again.
theme.noDatabase: The theme could not be kept, so it did not change: the application database is not open.
theme.notSaved: The theme could not be kept, so it did not change: {{reason}}
theme.unavailable: The theme can't be chosen in this window.

threshold.title: Warning threshold
threshold.hint: Usage marks an account's plan in warning from this share
threshold.description: The share of a 5-hour or weekly window at which plan limits count as nearly used. Limits belong to your accounts, so one value serves every project.
threshold.invalid: Use a whole percentage from 1 to 100.
threshold.unreadable: The warning threshold can't be read: {{reason}}

errorReports.label: Send error reports
errorReports.hint: Errors and crashes go to Orchester's error tracker, without secrets, prompts, file contents or project names
errorReports.unreadable: Whether to send error reports can't be read: {{reason}}
errorReports.notSaved: Changed until Orchester closes, but not saved, so it starts with the setting it had: {{reason}}
errorReports.notOpened: The page could not be opened. It is {{url}}

data.title: Application data
data.description: Settings, servers and the list of projects. Each project keeps its own data in its folder.
